newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ekran requotes lower after rights news.
newsitem.headline: Ekran requotes lower after rights news.

text.p: Shares of Bakun dam promoter Ekran Bhd requoted lower on Thursday following news that its rights issue of 257.1 million shares was undersubscribed by 62.77 percent.
At 0144 GMT, the stock was off 10 cents to 5.40 ringgit, its low so far for the session. Ekran's stock had been suspended on Tuesday pending a company announcement.
"A lot of it (the disinterest in the rights) has to do with the Bakun project," said the head of research at a local brokerage firm, referring to the $6.2 billion dam.
"People are a bit skeptical of Bakun," he said. The project has drawn fire from environmentalists concerned about damage to the rain forests where it is being built in Sarawak state.
Some investors, particularly foreign fund managers, have also shunned the project's stock offering because of the six year wait before earnings materialise.
The poor subscription rate forced Ting Phek Khiing, executive chairman of Ekran, to buy the 150.98 million unsubscribed shares at a total cost of 859.8 million ringgit ($341.9 million).
Ekran said in a statement issued by its merchant bankers that Ting's purchase price of the one-for-one rights issue was at 5.70 ringgit a share.
"This acquisition will increase the aggregate shareholdings of Tan Sri Ting and his spouse in Ekran from 26.3 percent to 55.7 percent," the statement said.
The 2,400 megawatt capacity Bakun dam would clear 69,000 hectares of forests, displace more than 9,000 tribal residents and create a reservoir the size of Singapore.
It is due to be finished by 2003 and preparatory work was started in 1996.
Stocks related to Ting showed a mixed performance on Thursday. His purchase of more Ekran shares raised speculation that he would restructure his holdings in his other companies for financing.
Granite Industries Bhd slipped six cents to 3.54 ringgit, PWE Industries Bhd was untraded after closing at 37.75 ringgit on Wednesday and Pacific Chemicals Bhd fell five cents to 6.10 ringgit.
